payload.text:
Short answer: the cut-outs are most likely two deterministic bugs in the app's own controller plumbing, not the iPad running out of headroom. And no, there is nothing today that records input timing, so latency itself cannot be tracked from the current build.

**How a stick reaches Dolphin** (I traced the full chain, including the two submodules that aren't checked out in this worktree, by fetching the exact commits the `jit-spike` build pins):

1. GameController HID callbacks land in DeltaCore's `MFiGameController` on a dedicated off-main queue. Each axis change becomes "deactivate the opposite direction, activate this direction with a value".
2. Stick samples go through DeltaCore's `AnalogInputCoalescer`, which keeps the last sample per input and flushes them all to the main thread once per run-loop pass.
3. On main, `NGCEmulatorBridge` in `ManicEmu/ManicEmu/Sources/Tools/Cores/NGC.swift` turns the direction values back into an (x, y) point and calls RetroArch's stick setter for that player.
4. RetroArch's `manic_joypad` driver stores it in per-port arrays. Dolphin reads them once per frame. The whole Dolphin frame also runs on the main thread, driven by a CADisplayLink.

**Bug 1, stick state shared across players** (`NGC.swift:123-124`). The bridge is a singleton with one `leftThumbstickPosition` and one `rightThumbstickPosition` for everyone. When player 2 pushes right, the bridge sends player 2's x together with whatever y player 1 last set. When player 1 lets go, the component is zeroed and sent for player 1, and player 2's held deflection is now gone from the shared state too. That is exactly "both sticks at once, each controller cuts out". It only shows with two or more controllers, which is why single-player feels fine. Upstream Manic EMU has the same code, and the Wii, N64, PS1, DOS, Arcade, Amiga and C64 bridges share the pattern.

**Bug 2, unordered flush.** The coalescer flushes a Swift dictionary, so a flick through center within one busy frame can deliver "activate right" before "deactivate left", leaving the stick at zero while it's held hard over until the player wiggles it. Longer Dolphin frames batch more events per flush, so a loaded minigame makes this more frequent, but it's a frontend bug, not a performance limit.

**Is the iPad being pushed too far?** Not by these symptoms. An M4 iPad Air is far from GameCube's ceiling with JIT on. Without JIT the interpreter runs at a reduced clock and frames can exceed 16 ms, which adds one frame of input delay through the main-thread hop above, but it would degrade smoothly rather than make a held stick read zero. The session log in `Documents/Netplay Logs/Manic MP sessions.log` says which mode each session ran in, so you can check whether JIT was actually on during that Mario Party session.

**Observability today:**

- Every Dolphin launch on the installed build writes a RetroArch INFO log plus one run-mode line. Useful for "was JIT on", nothing more.
- Frame-time stats exist only inside a connected netplay session.
- No input event is ever timestamped. Nothing reads Apple's per-controller `lastEventLatency`, nothing measures the hop to main, and the app's own debug logging is compiled out of release builds.
- Also noted: audio latency is set to 200 ms at launch, which adds perceived lag without causing drop-outs.

I saved the traced path and both bugs to the shared Track memory. The card above offers two next steps: fix the per-player state and ordered flush (the likely cure), and add input timing to the session log so the remaining latency can be measured rather than guessed.

Sources: [Apple, Handling input events](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/gamecontroller/handling-input-events), [Apple, lastEventTimestamp](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/gamecontroller/gcphysicalinputprofile/lasteventtimestamp)

**The shape.** A Linux box cannot compile an iOS app, so the build has to run on a rented Mac. The cheapest one is a GitHub-hosted macOS runner. All three repos involved are public forks under your account, so those minutes are free.

1. **Trigger.** A workflow in the Manic fork runs on a push to `jit-spike`, or on demand. A Track can start it for you.

3. **Hand-off.** The runner publishes the app package as a build artifact. The Pi pulls it with the GitHub login it already has and drops it in the signer's inbox. Nothing reaches into the Pi from outside.
4. **Sign and install.** The existing Pi signer takes over unchanged. It signs with your Apple session and upgrades the app on the iPad over the tailnet or home Wi-Fi.

End to end, that makes a change go from a merged pull request to the iPad without the Mac being on.

- **Xcode version.** The runner's Xcode must build this project as your Mac's does.

payload.command:
git status --short | grep -v '^??'; git log --oneline -1; mkdir -p .github/workflows && cat > .github/workflows/build-sideload.yml <<'EOF'
# Manic MP: build the sideload app on a GitHub-hosted Mac, with no Apple account.
#
# The Pi signer (better-games signer/) signs and installs the fork on the iPad,
# but nothing on Linux can compile it. This job is the compile step: it builds
# the ManicEmuSideload scheme for a device with signing switched off and
# publishes the result as the `manic-ipa` artifact, which the Pi pulls
# (signer/fetch-build.sh) and re-signs with the real team.
#
# No secret is used or needed here, and none may be added: the Apple ID lives
# on the Pi only. The repository is public, so hosted macOS minutes are free.
#
#   push to jit-spike     builds the iPad branch
#   push to build/<name>  builds any branch pushed under that prefix
#   Run workflow (ref)    builds any branch, tag or commit, from main's copy of
#                         this file
name: Build Manic MP (unsigned)

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      ref:
        description: Branch, tag or commit to build
        required: true
        default: jit-spike
  push:
    branches:
      - jit-spike
      - 'build/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: build-sideload-${{ github.event.inputs.ref || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  build:
    name: ManicEmuSideload, unsigned
    runs-on: macos-26
    timeout-minutes: 150
    env:
      BUNDLE_ID: com.globocodes.manicemu
      DERIVED_DATA: ${{ runner.temp }}/DerivedData
      OUT: ${{ runner.temp }}/out
    steps:
      - name: Check out the app, its submodules and the LFS cores
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.inputs.ref || github.sha }}
          submodules: recursive
          lfs: true

      - name: Select the newest Xcode 26
        run: |
          xcode="$(ls -d /Applications/Xcode_26*.app 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -1)"
          if [ -z "$xcode" ]; then
            echo "::error::No Xcode 26 on this runner image (the project is kept on Xcode 26)."
            ls -d /Applications/Xcode*.app
            exit 1
          fi
          sudo xcode-select -s "$xcode"
          xcodebuild -version
          xcodebuild -showsdks | grep -i iphoneos

      - name: Verify the LFS files are real content
        run: |
          git lfs ls-files | wc -l
          bash Scripts/VerifyLFS.sh
          du -sh Cores System.core

      - name: Build for a device, signing off
        run: |
          mkdir -p "$OUT"
          start=$(date +%s)
          set +e
          xcodebuild build \
            -project ManicEmu/ManicEmu.xcodeproj \
            -scheme ManicEmuSideload \
            -configuration SideloadRelease \
            -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' \
            -derivedDataPath "$DERIVED_DATA" \
            -skipPackagePluginValidation -skipMacroValidation \
            CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="" \
            > "$OUT/xcodebuild.log" 2>&1
          status=$?
          set -e
          echo "xcodebuild exited $status after $(( ($(date +%s) - start) / 60 )) min"
          if [ "$status" -ne 0 ]; then
            grep -nE "error:|fatal error|Undefined symbols|ld: |Command .* failed|BUILD FAILED" -A4 "$OUT/xcodebuild.log" | tail -150
            exit "$status"
          fi
          tail -3 "$OUT/xcodebuild.log"

      - name: Package Payload/ as manic.ipa
        run: |
          app="$(find "$DERIVED_DATA/Build/Products" -maxdepth 2 -name '*.app' -path '*-iphoneos/*' | head -1)"
          test -d "$app"
          id="$(/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c 'Print :CFBundleIdentifier' "$app/Info.plist")"
          version="$(/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c 'Print :CFBundleShortVersionString' "$app/Info.plist")"
          if [ "$id" != "$BUNDLE_ID" ]; then
            echo "::error::built $id, expected $BUNDLE_ID"
            exit 1
          fi

          # The Pi's signer asks Apple for the capabilities it finds in the main
          # binary's entitlements. A build with signing off carries none, so the
          # increased memory limit would only survive while the app id happens to
          # keep it. An ad-hoc signature (no account, no identity) puts the fork's
          # sideload entitlements into the binary; the Pi replaces the signature.
          codesign --force --deep --sign - "$app"
          codesign --force --sign - --entitlements ManicEmu/ManicEmu/ManicEmu-Sideload.entitlements "$app"
          codesign -d --entitlements - "$app" 2>/dev/null | grep -c increased-memory-limit

          work="$RUNNER_TEMP/ipa"
          mkdir -p "$work/Payload"
          cp -R "$app" "$work/Payload/"
          (cd "$work" && zip -qry "$OUT/manic.ipa" Payload)
          {
            echo "ref: ${{ github.event.inputs.ref || github.ref_name }}"
            echo "commit: $(git rev-parse HEAD)"
            echo "subject: $(git log -1 --format=%s)"
            echo "libretro: $(git -C Dependencies/Libretro rev-parse HEAD)"
            echo "deltacore: $(git -C Dependencies/DeltaCore rev-parse HEAD)"
            echo "version: $version"
            echo "xcode: $(xcodebuild -version | tr '\n' ' ')"
            echo "built: $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
            echo "sha256: $(shasum -a 256 "$OUT/manic.ipa" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
          } | tee "$OUT/build-info.txt"
          ls -lh "$OUT/manic.ipa"

      - name: Upload manic.ipa
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: manic-ipa
          path: |
            ${{ env.OUT }}/manic.ipa
            ${{ env.OUT }}/build-info.txt
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14
          compression-level: 0

      - name: Upload the build log
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: xcodebuild-log
          path: ${{ env.OUT }}/xcodebuild.log
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 7
EOF

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Pull a Mac-free build of the Manic fork from GitHub and hand it to the signer.
#
#   fetch-build.sh [--branch <name> | --run <id>] [--dry-run]
#
# The fork's "Build Manic MP (unsigned)" workflow (globocodes/ManicEMU,
# .github/workflows/build-sideload.yml) compiles the app on a GitHub-hosted Mac
# with no Apple account and publishes it as the `manic-ipa` artifact. This
# downloads that artifact with this machine's own gh login, checks it, and
# runs resign.sh on it. Nothing reaches into the Pi from outside.
#
#   --branch   the branch whose newest successful run to take (default jit-spike)
#   --run      one specific run id instead
#   --dry-run  sign and check only. The build stays in inbox/staged/,
#              inbox/manic.ipa is untouched and nothing is sent to the iPad.

# kept as inbox/manic.ipa.prev) and is installed on the iPad as an upgrade.
# The daily job re-signs whatever inbox/manic.ipa holds, so from then on it
# keeps this build signed.
#
# --dry-run still signs, which talks to Apple with the saved session. The
# bundle id is fixed below and is never taken from the download.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
. ./env.sh

repo="${MANIC_BUILD_REPO:-globocodes/ManicEMU}"
workflow="build-sideload.yml"
artifact="manic-ipa"
bundle_id="com.globocodes.manicemu"

branch="jit-spike"
run=""
mode=""
while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
        --branch) branch="${2:?--branch needs a name}"; shift 2 ;;
        --run) run="${2:?--run needs an id}"; shift 2 ;;
        --dry-run) mode="--dry-run"; shift ;;
        *) echo "usage: $0 [--branch <name> | --run <id>] [--dry-run]" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    esac
done

command -v gh >/dev/null || { echo "gh is not installed or not on PATH" >&2; exit 6; }

if [ -z "$run" ]; then
    run="$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow "$workflow" --branch "$branch" \
        --status success --limit 1 --json databaseId --jq '.[0].databaseId // empty')"
    if [ -z "$run" ]; then
        echo "No successful $workflow run on $branch in $repo." >&2
        exit 1
    fi
fi
gh run view "$run" --repo "$repo" --json headBranch,headSha,conclusion,createdAt,workflowName \
    --jq '"run '"$run"': \(.workflowName), \(.headBranch) @ \(.headSha[0:8]), \(.conclusion), \(.createdAt)"'

umask 077
staged_dir="$SIGNER_HOME/inbox/staged"
mkdir -p "$staged_dir"
work="$(mktemp -d "$staged_dir/.fetch.XXXXXX")"

gh run download "$run" --repo "$repo" --name "$artifact" --dir "$work"
ipa="$work/manic.ipa"
info="$work/build-info.txt"

python3 - "$ipa" "$info" "$bundle_id" <<'PY'
import hashlib, plistlib, re, sys, zipfile

ipa, info_path, bundle_id = sys.argv[1:4]
digest = hashlib.sha256(open(ipa, "rb").read()).hexdigest()
try:
    recorded = dict(line.split(": ", 1) for line in open(info_path).read().splitlines() if ": " in line)
except OSError:
    recorded = {}
want = recorded.get("sha256")
if want and want != digest:
    sys.exit(f"sha256 mismatch: artifact says {want}, download is {digest}")
z = zipfile.ZipFile(ipa)
name = next((n for n in z.namelist() if re.fullmatch(r"Payload/[^/]+\.app/Info\.plist", n)), None)
if name is None:
    sys.exit("no Payload/<app>/Info.plist in the package")
plist = plistlib.loads(z.read(name))
if plist.get("CFBundleIdentifier") != bundle_id:
    sys.exit(f"package is {plist.get('CFBundleIdentifier')}, not {bundle_id}")
for key in ("ref", "commit", "subject", "libretro", "deltacore", "xcode", "built"):

PY

commit="$(sed -n 's/^commit: //p' "$info" 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-8)"
staged="$staged_dir/manic-${commit:-run$run}.ipa"
mv "$ipa" "$staged"
[ -f "$info" ] && mv "$info" "$staged.info"
echo "staged: $staged"

if [ "$mode" = "--dry-run" ]; then
    exec ./resign.sh "$staged" "$bundle_id" --dry-run
fi

inbox="$SIGNER_HOME/inbox/manic.ipa"
[ -f "$inbox" ] && mv -f "$inbox" "$inbox.prev"
cp "$staged" "$inbox"
echo "inbox/manic.ipa is now this build (previous kept as manic.ipa.prev)"
exec ./resign.sh "$inbox" "$bundle_id"
EOF

payload.text:
The Pi's better-games checkout is on main with the fetch script, but the test run is not fully green: one test fails, for a reason unrelated to the pull.

- **Status before pulling:** clean, on `main`.
- **Pull:** fast-forward to `4fa7267`, the merge of PR #20. It changed three files, all under `signer/`.
- **Venv:** `.venv/bin/gct` already existed, so no reinstall.
- **`gct env`:** exit 0. It resolved the repo, the library, the work directory on ext4, both Dolphin tools and the Redump data file with 2268 entries.
- **Tests:** 1 failed, 69 passed, 3 skipped.

| Outcome | Test | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Failed | `tests/test_move_homes.py::test_apply_edits_the_real_archives_once` | See below |
| Skipped | `test_arc.py`, `test_iff.py` | No G4ME69 extraction under `GCT_WORK` |
| Skipped | `test_yaz0.py` | Needs `GCT_SLOW=1` |

**The failure is the state of the work tree, not this pull.** The test applies the "Move homes" recipe to copies of two Animal Crossing archives and asserts that both change. On the Pi, the extraction under `~/incoming/gct-work/GAFE01` already carries that edit: both archives were rewritten on October 1. I applied the recipe to copies and neither file changed, so the assertion fails. The format round-trip tests all pass.

I did not re-extract the disc to make it green, because that tree holds another Track's in-place edits. A pristine extraction in a separate `GCT_WORK` would clear it. I saved this to the shared memory so the next Track does not read it as a regression.

The installed `fetch-build.sh` on the Pi matches main byte for byte.
